name: GSEMA — Technology Platform Strategy Assessment
description:
Girl Scouts of Eastern Massachusetts (GSEMA) issued an RFP for a comprehensive technology platform strategy assessment. The engagement covers three phases:

Phase 1: Discovery & Needs Analysis — stakeholder interviews (10-15 people), system audit of all hardware/software/data storage, and needs prioritization
Phase 2: Analysis & Future State Definition — gap analysis, solution identification (2-3 nonprofit-friendly integrated platforms), and future state architecture roadmap
Phase 3: Documentation & Presentation — assessment report, prioritized recommendations, technical architecture diagram, and 12-month implementation roadmap with budget

GSEMA serves ~20,000 girls and 9,000 volunteers across Eastern MA. Their core challenge is fragmented systems across membership, finance, volunteer management, and donor/fundraising — data siloed in Salesforce, Raiser's Edge, Abila MIP, Google Workspace, Campminder, and multiple auxiliary tools.

RFP submission deadline was 2026-02-27. Finalist interviews scheduled March 9-11, selection March 16, project kickoff target March 30.

Even if Phase I assessment is awarded, Phases II (Systems Selection) and III (Implementation) represent follow-on engagement opportunities.
mutual_commitments: Wright Adventures would provide technology assessment and strategic roadmap services. Deliverables: technology assessment report, prioritized recommendations, future state technical architecture, and phased implementation roadmap with estimated budget. GSEMA provides stakeholder access, system documentation, and $50K project budget.
alignment_notes: Strong alignment with Strategic Objective 6 (Democratize Technology Access) — this is exactly the kind of technology consulting engagement Wright Adventures' "Scale With Technology" practice is designed to deliver. GSEMA's youth development mission aligns with WA's core focus areas. Successful delivery would serve as a flagship case study for the Technology & Innovation consulting practice and could lead to Phase II/III implementation work.

name: Climate Democracy Initiative (CDI) — Partnership
description: CDI is a nonprofit working at the intersection of climate change and democratic governance. The organization works to rebuild public trust, local leadership, and systems that include people most affected by climate change. CDI operates three main program areas: Community Visioning for energy development decisions and resilience planning, Empowering the Next Generation of Environmental Leaders through educational partnerships, and Narrative and Policy Change to strengthen public understanding of climate and democracy as shared issues.
ai_match_rationale: CDI is a climate-focused organization seeking communications and funder storytelling infrastructure — work that sits naturally on top of systems (newsletter platforms, donor CRMs, content pipelines) where Wright Adventures can propose a more durable solution than a solo contractor would; betterbikeshare.org and kadysheepcamp.org offer credible analogues on both the funder-narrative and small-org axes. The strongest reason not to pursue is that this posting is written as a solo-practitioner role with no stated budget, no technical framing, and no existing relationship — making it a cold, uncertain-value bid against a brief that does not yet know a firm could answer it.

name: City Thread
description:
Zoho CRM Consultant 
Request for Proposal 

City Thread is seeking a skilled CRM consultant to support the setup, design, and integration of Zoho CRM Plus, its CRM platform. The overarching goal is to enhance donor engagement, streamline fundraising, marketing, and fee-for-service processes and revenue, and improve data-driven decision-making.
